source_name: Banka CREDITAS – owned site (tiskové zprávy / o bance)
why_relevant: CREDITAS grew fast by acquisition (Max banka/Expobank CZ) and runs an internet-banking product that aggregates third-party accounts — migration and multibanking work implies concrete vendor decisions. Its own media/investor pages are the primary channel; it also has PSE-listed bonds, adding a disclosure obligation.

source_name: Erste Group – Press releases (parent of Česká spořitelna)
why_relevant: Group-level owned channel that announces platform decisions rolled out to ČS (e.g. group PSD2/open-banking API programme). Group press rooms often name vendors that the CZ subsidiary's own release omits.
Vendor-owned, filterable index of named bank references; enumerates CEE/CZ clients and dates deployments. One page yields multiple Czech actors and product names (Transact, Core, Data Hub).

Named CZ core-banking win: KB on Temenos Core + Data Hub since 2021, phased retail migration to 2025, private cloud on Kubernetes/PostgreSQL, LTIMindtree as SI. Dates, scope and integrator all in one artifact.

source_name: Businesswire press release — Komerční banka selects Temenos (Jan 2021)
why_relevant: Wire-distributed vendor announcement establishes the contract award date for the largest CZ core-banking replacement. Wire services are the canonical vendor-win channel and are archived.

source_name: Diebold Nixdorf Investor Relations press-release archive
why_relevant: Primary, dated archive of DN customer wins; contains the ČSOB tellerless-branch/DN AllConnect Managed Services release (2022, 1,025 self-service devices, relationship since 2001) and the DN Series 300 launch naming Komerční banka as pilot.

source_name: ATM Marketplace — Diebold Nixdorf company media hub
why_relevant: Trade-press aggregator that republishes vendor self-service/ATM announcements per company, including a Czech bank contactless deployment. Useful when the vendor newsroom prunes old releases.

source_name: Kiosk Marketplace — Czech self-service/branch automation coverage
why_relevant: Sister trade title carrying the same vendor releases with different headlines/metadata; useful redundancy and occasionally adds device counts and branch-format detail.

Post-split ATM incumbent's own announcement channel; CZ appears in its contactless-ATM and ATM-as-a-Service country lists, implying named CZ deployments to be traced. Also the place where any Brink's-era ownership change would be disclosed.

Deepest single vein of named CZ bank outsourcing wins found in this cell: Česká spořitelna (prepaid recharge), Citibank CZ ATM outsourcing, Bank Austria Creditanstalt CZ ATM operations, ABN AMRO CZ card+ATM outsourcing, Oskar ATM recharge. Long historical archive dates each deal.

Euronet's independent-ATM-deployer arm publishes CZ-market-specific statements (e.g. rebutting claims in the Czech market), revealing regulatory/PR friction and its CZ market posture rather than client wins.

Czech-language vendor reference list; the classic 'one page enumerates a dozen clients' pointer. Asseco's banking segment names Česká spořitelna among customers; the CZ site also lists public-sector and financial references.

Vendor annual reports narrate CZ contract wins and segment revenue by client type — often naming banks that never appear in a case study. Historic PDFs give a longitudinal view of the CZ banking IT install base.

source_name: Národní elektronický nástroj (NEN) supplier registry — vendor entity pages
why_relevant: Surfaced while chasing Asseco: the CZ supplier registry gives a vendor's registered CZ legal entity, which is the key to linking a global vendor's marketing claims to local contracting entities (and to any public-sector contracts). Cross-cell bridge from vendor-owned content into procurement data.
Backbase publishes named CEE wins (e.g. 365.bank in Slovakia, jointly with Mambu). Slovak/Polish neighbours are the leading indicator for CZ; any CZ engagement would surface here first.

Partner directories enumerate the SIs and technology partners that actually deliver CZ projects (Deloitte, Persistent, Backbase et al.); combining vendor + SI names yields far better CZ-specific search recall than vendor name alone.
Per-partner profiles reveal which SI delivers Temenos in CEE (LTIMindtree named on the KB engagement). Identifies the second party to any CZ deployment and gives a second newsroom to monitor.

Localized vendor country site — the natural home for CZ merchant-acquiring references, KB SmartPay alliance material and CZ partner/bank relationships. Country microsites frequently carry client logos absent from the global site.

Counterpart-side confirmation of vendor deals that vendor marketing states loosely: KB/Worldline merchant-acquiring alliance, the staged 80%/19%/1% sale of Worldline Czech Republic s.r.o. (EUR 27m, completed Dec 2025). Gives exact dates, stakes and legal entities — the hard data a case study omits.

Nexi is the consolidator of CEE acquiring/issuing assets; its dated release archive (with parallel Italian 'nota stampa' PDFs) is where any CZ bank partnership or portfolio acquisition would be announced first.

source_name: ACI Worldwide newsroom / investor press releases
why_relevant: ACI is a likely incumbent in CZ payment switching/real-time payments; its newsroom and the parallel investor feed are the only routes to named CZ wins, none of which surfaced in generic search.

Third-party mirrors of vendor case studies; they retain studies vendors have deleted and normalize them per vendor, making them a recovery route for withdrawn CZ references. Low authority, high pointer value.

source_name: Czech SI/consultancy case-study pages naming bank clients (Enehano, LLP CRM, eppTec)
why_relevant: Local implementation partners publish cs-language 'případové studie' naming the bank and the platform (Česká spořitelna/Salesforce — described as the largest CEE Salesforce implementation; Raiffeisenbank/Microsoft Dynamics CRM). These fill the gap where global vendors stay silent about CZ.

source_name: IBS Intelligence — core banking deal coverage (CZ)
why_relevant: Specialist banking-technology trade title that reports vendor selections independently and often adds contract context vendors omit; also runs sales-league tables that count CZ deals.

source_name: Trask (wearetrask.com / thetrask.com) — case studies & banking practice
why_relevant: Trask is the largest CZ-owned integrator embedded in Czech/Slovak retail banks (core banking, digital channels, PSD2/open banking, CRM). Its case-study and magazine content names bank clients (e.g. Komerční banka document platform, Slovenská sporiteľňa MS Dynamics CRM) that the banks themselves do not publicise, and reveals which sub-vendors and product stacks are used.

Adastra is the dominant data/BI integrator for CZ banks. Its Czech success-story pages name banks explicitly (Equa bank ODS + Adastra Banking Data Model, event-driven marketing in a leading Czech bank, Raiffeisenbank data platform), giving both project-level detail and the ABDM product footprint.

source_name: Adastra CZ careers site — case-study section (jobs.adastra.cz)
why_relevant: Recruitment microsites reuse project descriptions that legal has scrubbed from the corporate site, and job ads name the exact bank technology stack being staffed (ABDM, Teradata, Informatica, core banking). A leading indicator of new bank programmes 3-9 months before delivery.

Profinit publishes named bank engagements (REMOS receivables monitoring for ČSOB; long-running BI/DWH programme at Komerční banka since 2005; Česká spořitelna, Raiffeisenbank listed as clients). Directly reveals risk/BI system ownership inside the four largest CZ banks.
